name: Rattle Rows
idea: Full-width 1-row channels between block bands; the ball rattles along each band.
hint: Clear the blue bands from below. Break the blue guard under the red pot last.

name: Switchback
idea: A snake corridor: shelves with a gap at alternate ends. Breaking shelf blocks cuts shortcuts.
hint: Wind up through the shelves. The red pot waits at the top gap: finish blue first.

name: Pockets
idea: Two-cell pockets walled by blocks; the ball rattles inside and breaks into the next pocket.
hint: Blue only. Every pocket wall you break opens the next room.

name: Shafts
idea: Short vertical shafts between stone columns, linked by grey windows you carve sideways.
hint: Blue only. Bounce up a shaft, then break a grey window to cross over.

name: Grey Scaffold
idea: A grey lattice you carve through with coloured nuggets inside; you build your own corridors.
hint: Grey breaks in any colour. Blue first, then dig to the red pot in the middle.

name: Colour Onion
idea: Four colour layers stacked bottom to top; each layer's pot sits at the next layer's door.
hint: Blue, red, green, gold, from the bottom up. Each pot opens the layer above it.

name: Stone Heavy
idea: Close to the density reference: about a third of the field is stone, corridors are fixed.
hint: The stone never breaks. Find the route that touches the most blue.

name: Brick Wall
idea: Almost no stone: a solid wall of coloured bricks with a few grey ribs. You carve every corridor.
hint: Blue, then red from the pot at the right edge, then the diamonds.

name: Narrow Eight
idea: The rattle-row idea on an 8-column grid: bigger tiles on the phone, shorter channels.
hint: Clear the blue bands, then the red ones. The red pot hides behind the blue guard.

name: Open Field
idea: Contrast: sparse blocks and long flights, built for speed routes rather than corridors.
hint: Few blocks, lots of air. Find the fastest line through them.
